stages.title: Reading and writing fundamentals
stages.hook: Russian handwriting looks different from print. Which letter looks like an English m?
explain: In school, Russian children learn printed and cursive letters. In cursive the letter т looks like a small m, and д can look like a small g. Words are read from left to right, and each letter has a capital and a small form.

Russian spelling follows rules. After ж, ш, ч and щ write и, never ы: жизнь, шить. To spell an unstressed vowel, find a related word where it is stressed: вода (water) and воды (VO-dy) show that the first letter is о. Days and months do not have a capital letter: понедельник, май.
stages.mnemonic: To check a weak vowel, make it strong: вода, воды, so write о.
sentences: The teacher writes on the board.

gq.why: After ж one writes и, not ы.

gq.q: How can you check the unstressed vowel in вода?
o: Look at a related word with stress, such as воды
gq.why: A strong form shows the real vowel: вОды has о.

panel.q: Which is written with a small first letter in Russian?
panel.why: Days of the week and months are not capitalised, while names of countries and people are.

panel.q: Why does Russian say и not ы after ш?
o: Because и is a new letter
It is a spelling rule: ы is not written after ж, ш, ч and щ
Because ы is only for questions
panel.why: These letters are always followed by и in spelling, even if sounds seem similar.

panel.q: The soft sign in тетрадь does not have its own sound. What does it show?
o: That the noun is in the plural
That the word is a question
panel.why: Ь marks softness of the consonant before it.

teach.model: Russian spelling follows rules. After ж, ш, ч and щ write и. For unstressed vowels, find a related word where the vowel is stressed, like вода and воды. Days and months are written with small letters.

points.ask: Is there a rule for spelling?
How do I check a weak vowel?

trip.prompt: Find one spelling rule and make your own example word.

stages.title: Basic sentence construction
stages.hook: In Russian "Мама любит Аню" and "Аню любит мама" mean the same. How do we know who loves whom?
explain: A simple Russian sentence has a subject and a verb: Мама читает. Word order is flexible because endings tell the role. In Мама любит Аню, мама is the subject and Аню (with -у) is the object.
Join ideas with и (and), а (and, but in contrast), но (but) and потому что (because). A comma goes before а, но and потому что. In the present, a dash can replace "is": Москва — столица России.
stages.mnemonic: Endings are labels on the words: -у marks the object, no matter where it stands.
sentences: Mum is at home, and dad is at work.
I like tea but do not like coffee.

gq.q: In Аню любит мама, who loves?
gq.why: Мама is in the subject form and Аню is the object.

gq.q: Where does не go to make a verb negative?
o: After the verb: Я знаю не
At the end of the sentence
Before the verb: Я не знаю
gq.why: Не stands directly before the word it negates.

panel.q: Why can Russian change word order more freely than English?
o: Russian has no fixed grammar rules at all
Case endings show each word's role
panel.why: Because endings show roles, word order can show emphasis instead.

panel.q: Which conjunction fits: Я люблю чай, ___ не люблю кофе?
panel.why: Но introduces a contrast with what was said before.

panel.q: In Москва — столица России, what does the dash replace?
o: The word "capital", which is left out
panel.why: Russian omits "is" in the present and may use a dash.

teach.model: A Russian sentence has a subject and a verb. Word order is flexible because the endings show who does what. Join ideas with и, а, но and потому что and put a comma before а, но and потому что.

points.ask: What do I need in a sentence?

trip.prompt: Find a sentence with different word order and explain what changes.

stages.title: Common verbs
stages.hook: English has one verb "go". Russian has more. Which would you use to walk, and which to travel by bus?
explain: Useful verbs: делать (to do), хотеть (to want), мочь (to be able), знать (to know), жить (to live), любить (to love). Some are irregular. Хотеть: я хочу, ты хочешь, он хочет, мы хотим, они хотят.

Russian splits "to go". Идти means to go on foot, and ехать means to go by vehicle. Я иду в школу means "I am walking to school", Я еду в школу на автобусе means "I am going to school by bus". After хочу or люблю use the infinitive: Я хочу пить.

gq.q: Which verb fits "I go to school by bus"?
gq.why: Ехать is used for travel by vehicle.

gq.q: Which is the correct form of хотеть?
gq.why: Хотеть is irregular: хочу, хочешь, хочет.

panel.q: Why does Russian use two verbs for "to go"?
o: It shows whether the speaker is a man or a woman
It shows how you move: on foot or by vehicle
panel.why: Verbs of motion encode manner and direction.

panel.q: Which sentence is correct?
panel.why: After люблю the second verb is an infinitive.

panel.q: Why is "они хотят" not "они хочут"?
o: Because хотеть is a noun that takes a plural ending
It is an irregular verb with changed endings
panel.why: Хотеть mixes two conjugation types.

teach.model: Russian has irregular verbs like хотеть: хочу, хочешь, хочет. There are two verbs for going: идти for walking and ехать for vehicles. After хочу use an infinitive.

points.ask: What are the forms of хотеть?

trip.prompt: Find the verbs of motion table and mark идти and ехать.

stages.title: Nouns, pronouns and modifiers
stages.hook: The Russian word "it" does not exist for things. How would you say "it" about a table?
explain: Pronouns: я, ты, он, она, оно, мы, вы, они. Nouns also use он, она, оно according to gender: стол — он, книга — она, окно — оно. Do not think of "it" as a Russian word for objects.
Adjectives, "my" and "this" must match the noun: большая комната (feminine), большой дом (masculine), большое окно (neuter). Plural adjectives are the same for all genders: большие дома.
stages.mnemonic: Every table is a "he", every book is a "she".

gq.q: Which pronoun do you use for книга?

gq.why: Комната is feminine, so the adjective ends in -ая.

panel.q: Why is a table called он in Russian?
panel.why: Pronouns follow the grammatical gender of the noun.

panel.q: Why is вы both polite and plural?
o: Russian uses the plural form to show respect
panel.why: Вы works as one polite "you" or as many people.

panel.q: In the plural, what happens to gender in adjectives?
o: Three forms remain, as in the singular
The form is the same for all genders
panel.why: Plural adjectives take one ending, like -ие.

teach.model: Use я, ты, он, она, оно, мы, вы, они. Он, она and оно are also used for things according to gender. Adjectives agree with their noun: большой дом, большая комната.

points.ask: What do I call a thing?

trip.prompt: Find the table of personal pronouns and say them in a row.

stages.title: Questions and responses
stages.hook: If someone asks "Ты любишь чай?", can you answer with only one word?
explain: Question words: кто (who), что (what), где (where), когда (when), почему (why), как (how), сколько (how many), куда (where to). Где asks about place and куда asks about direction: Где ты? and Куда ты идёшь?

A yes/no question has the same words as a statement and rising voice on the key word. Answer with Да, люблю (yes, I love) by repeating the verb, or Нет, не люблю. Russian uses double negatives: Я ничего не знаю is correct.
stages.mnemonic: Где = at a place, куда = to a place.

gq.q: How do you answer Ты любишь чай? with a full yes?
gq.why: Russians often repeat the verb in the first person.

panel.q: Why is "Я ничего не знаю" not wrong, although it has two negatives?
o: Two negatives cancel each other, but only in Russian
Russian requires the negative word with не
panel.why: Double negation is standard grammar in Russian.

panel.q: Why do you say Где ты? but Куда ты идёшь?
o: They are the same word with two spellings
Куда asks about the goal of movement
panel.why: Where is it? vs where are you going?

panel.q: A yes/no question needs which spoken signal in Russian?
o: A special question word at the end
Rising intonation on the key word
panel.why: Intonation marks the question when no question word is used.

teach.model: Use кто, что, где, когда, почему, как, сколько and куда. Где asks about place and куда about direction. A yes/no question has rising voice.

points.ask: How do I ask a yes/no question?

trip.prompt: Find the question words in a list and make a question with each.

stages.title: Describing people and places
stages.hook: Would you say "в улице" or "на улице"? Russians choose carefully.
explain: To describe a person say: Мой брат высокий. Words like добрый (kind), весёлый (cheerful), красивый (beautiful), новый (new), старый (old) change their ending: моя сестра высокая.
For places we use в for inside spaces: в городе, в деревне. We use на for open places and events: на улице, на работе. Вот is a short word for "here is".
stages.mnemonic: В is inside the box, на is on the surface.
sentences: In the village it is quiet and calm.

gq.q: How do you say "My sister is tall"?
gq.why: The adjective takes the feminine ending to match сестра.

panel.q: Why do we say в городе but на работе?
o: Prepositions в and на follow usage; на is used for open spaces and activities
There is no reason at all
panel.why: The choice follows convention with patterns.

panel.q: After в, the noun город changes to городе. What is this form called?
panel.why: The prepositional case is used after в and на for location.

panel.q: Why is the adjective in в красивом городе different from красивый город?
o: It agrees with the noun in case as well as gender
panel.why: Adjectives change with the case of the noun.

teach.topic: Describing people and places in Russian
teach.model: Adjectives match the noun: мой брат высокий, моя сестра высокая. Use в for places inside and на for open spaces or activities: в городе, на улице.

trip.prompt: Find examples with в and на and sort them into two groups.

stages.title: Time, dates and daily routines
stages.hook: In Russia the school week starts on Monday. Can you say what day it is today?
explain: Time words: утро (morning), день (day), вечер (evening), неделя (week), месяц (month), год (year). Days: понедельник, вторник, среда, четверг, пятница, суббота, воскресенье. They are written with small letters.
To say a day use в plus the accusative: в понедельник (on Monday). For clock times say в семь часов (at seven o'clock). Ask Который час? or Сколько времени? to find the time.
stages.mnemonic: Days of the week are written with small letters: понедельник, вторник, среда.
sentences: I get up at seven o'clock.
The lesson begins in the morning.

gq.why: Days use в with the accusative.

gq.q: How do you ask the time?
gq.why: Который час? and Сколько времени? both ask the time.

panel.q: Which day follows вторник?
panel.why: The order is вторник, среда, четверг.

panel.q: Why is it "в семь часов" with часов?
o: After seven the noun часы takes a plural genitive form
panel.why: After numbers from five the noun uses the genitive plural.

panel.q: Which is NOT a normal way to write a day name in Russian?
o: Понедельник with a capital letter in the middle of a sentence
panel.why: Days are written with small letters except at sentence start.

teach.model: Days are written with small letters: понедельник, вторник, среда. To say on a day use в: в понедельник. Say clock time with в and часов: в семь часов.

points.ask: How do I say on Monday?
How do I say the time?

trip.prompt: Find the names of months and list the first three.

sources: Names of days of the week

stages.title: Food and shopping
stages.hook: How do you politely ask a shopkeeper for one apple?
explain: Food and shop words: хлеб (bread), суп (soup), яблоко (apple), сыр (cheese), магазин (shop), цена (price), рубль (rouble). Ask Сколько это стоит? (How much is this?).

To ask for something politely say Дайте, пожалуйста, ... After numbers the word рубль changes: один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей. In Russian culture bread and salt (хлеб-соль) are a traditional sign of welcome for guests.
stages.mnemonic: Дайте, пожалуйста: the magic words in a shop.

gq.q: Which phrase is polite for asking in a shop?

gq.why: After five and more use the genitive plural рублей.

panel.q: Why is it два рубля but пять рублей?
o: The form depends on the number
Рубль is actually two different words
panel.why: Numbers 2 to 4 take genitive singular and 5 or more take genitive plural.

panel.q: Which question is a polite way to ask a price?
panel.why: Скажите, пожалуйста is polite.

panel.q: Why does a word like яблоко end in -о?
panel.why: Nouns ending in -о are usually neuter.

teach.model: Ask politely with Дайте, пожалуйста. Ask the price with Сколько это стоит? Rubles change after numbers: один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей.

points.ask: How do I ask the price?

trip.prompt: Find a traditional dish and note its Russian name.

stages.title: Everyday conversations
stages.hook: You meet a new friend. Which questions can you ask to get to know them?
explain: Useful questions are Откуда ты? (Where are you from?) and Что нового? (What is new?). To answer say Я из Нигерии, Я из Ганы or Я из Бразилии. The word из takes the genitive: Нигерия becomes из Нигерии.
Say goodbye with Увидимся! (See you!) and wish Хорошего дня! (Have a good day!). The reply is И вам тоже! (To you too!). With friends you can say Давай встретимся (Let us meet), which is informal.
stages.mnemonic: Из means "from" and takes the genitive: из Ганы, из Нигерии, из Бразилии.

gq.q: What is a polite reply to Хорошего дня?
gq.why: И вам тоже is the polite reply.

gq.q: Which form is correct for "I am from Brazil" (Бразилия)?
gq.why: Из is followed by the genitive.

panel.q: Which sentence is informal?
panel.why: Давай is the informal singular form.

panel.q: Why does Russian say Я из Ганы and not Я из Гана?
o: Гана is a verb that changes form
panel.why: The genitive ending -ы replaces -а in Гана.

panel.q: What does the reflexive ending -ся in увидимся suggest?
o: The action is mutual: we see each other
panel.why: The -ся form can express reciprocal action.

teach.model: Ask Откуда ты? and answer Я из Ганы. Say Увидимся! for see you and Хорошего дня! for have a good day. The reply is И вам тоже!

points.ask: How do I ask where someone is from?
How do I say where I am from?
How do I say see you?

trip.prompt: Find a short dialogue and read it aloud with a friend.
